label: generic
text: Can I see the V5C log book? Does the name and address match yours, and do the VIN and engine number match the car?
why: The V5C shows the registered keeper. It's not proof of ownership, but mismatches are a warning sign.

label: generic
text: Has it had a history check for outstanding finance, theft or a write-off (insurance category)? Can I run one?
why: A car with outstanding finance can be repossessed from the new owner. History checks also show write-offs and theft markers.

label: generic
text: Can I look up the MOT history? Have the advisories been fixed, and does the mileage go up steadily?
why: GOV.UK's free MOT history shows past fails, advisories and recorded mileage, which helps spot clocking or recurring faults.

label: generic
text: Is there a full service history with stamps or invoices? When and at what mileage was it last serviced?
why: Service history shows whether the car has been maintained as the manufacturer requires.

label: generic
text: How many previous owners has it had, and how long have you owned it?
why: The V5C and history checks show keeper changes. A short ownership period is worth asking about.

label: generic
text: Are there any outstanding safety recalls on this car? Can I check the registration on GOV.UK?
why: GOV.UK has a free recall checker by make, model and VIN, and recall work is free at a dealer.

label: generic
text: Has it ever had accident damage, paint or bodywork repairs, or any modifications?
why: Undeclared repairs and modifications affect value and insurance. Check panel gaps and paint match.

label: generic
text: Does it come with two keys and the locking wheel nut key?
why: Missing keys are expensive to replace, and only one key can be a sign of a problem.

label: generic
text: Is any manufacturer or dealer warranty left, and does it transfer to me?
why: Warranty left can cover costly repairs, but check it transfers.

label: generic
text: When does the MOT run out?
why: A car with a short MOT may need work soon. Check the date on GOV.UK.

label: generic
text: Is it ULEZ / Clean Air Zone compliant? Can I check the reg on TfL's checker?
why: Non-compliant cars face daily charges in London's ULEZ and some other UK Clean Air Zones.

label: generic
text: How much tread is left on the tyres, and do they all match?
why: The legal minimum for cars is 1.6mm across the central three-quarters of the tread.

label: generic
text: When were the brake discs and pads last replaced? Any noises or pulling under braking?
why: Brakes are a safety-critical wear item and a common MOT failure point.

label: generic
text: Are any warning lights on the dashboard, and do all the electrics (windows, air con, lights) work?
why: Warning lights and electrical faults can be costly to diagnose and fix.

label: generic
why: Tax doesn't transfer to a new keeper, so you need to tax it before driving away. Check its status on GOV.UK.

label: generic
text: Does this engine have a timing belt or a chain? If it's a belt, when was it last changed and can I see the invoice?
why: A belt that snaps can cause major engine damage, so ask for proof of replacement.

label: generic
text: Can I start it from cold and take it for a test drive (on insurance that covers me)?
why: A cold start shows up rattles, smoke and starting problems. A test drive checks the clutch, gearbox, steering and brakes.
